name: Electron/Chromium 132: V8 page allocator assumes a 4K page, renderer crashes at runtime on 16K
component: Electron 34.0.2-34.2.x (Chromium 132/133) bundled in an app; V8 pooled-page decommit uses a hard-coded page size. Applies to VSCode, Obsidian, and any app bundling an Electron in this window
required_postconditions: V8's page pool manages memory in units of its compiled-in page size; the host page size must not exceed 4096 or the pooled-page decommit math addresses the wrong span and the renderer faults

failure_sink.description: RUNTIME crash, not a load failure: the binary loads and starts, then the renderer process crashes on a 16K-page host because Chromium 132 hard-coded a 4K page size in V8's pooled-page decommit. Workaround: --js-flags="--nodecommit_pooled_pages". This is what distinguishes Class B from the ELF-load-alignment class (MuseScore): ld.so is happy; V8 is not.

extraction_limitations: the real defect is a runtime V8 crash, not a page-size predicate the loader enforces. required_page_size at_most 4096 is the closest this schema can encode: it stands in for 'V8's page pool needs the host page to be at most its compiled-in 4096'. The static verdict is therefore a proxy for a runtime failure, the same modelling compromise as the redis --with-lg-page contract.
detection of a broken binary is by bundled Chromium version, NOT by ELF layout; this contract expresses the consequence, not the way you find an offender.

x_campaign.project: Electron / Chromium 132 (Class B - runtime, NOT ELF-load)
x_campaign.quote: crashes the renderer on systems using 16K pages due to an incorrect hard-coded page size
x_campaign.broken_window: Electron 34.0.2 - 34.2.x (Chromium 132-133). Fixed in 34.3.0+ / Chromium 134+. Safe at <= 33.3.2.
x_campaign.expected_verdict_by_host_rationale: required_page_size is at_most 4096. Only macos/aarch64+none measures a 16384 page, so RS-VM-0006 fires there and only there; every 4K host (linux, rosetta, windows) satisfies the bound. The historical incident was a 16K aarch64 LINUX host (Asahi/Pi5); macos/aarch64+none is the only measured 16K profile in this tree and stands in for it.
x_campaign.detection: NOT ldso_predicate.py (ELF is fine). Signal is the bundled Chromium version: strings <appbin> | grep -oiE 'Chrome/[0-9]+' -> 132 or 133 = broken window.
x_campaign.status: the CLASS is known/reported for VSCode, Obsidian, Vesktop. Novelty would be an app bundling a broken-window Electron with NO 16K issue of its own; the 2026-08 hunt found none still shipping in the broken window.
